quote: just first thing All I wanna know is what's the what's the, you know, general range of cost for something like that.
stewart_read: This is a price_estimate_before_design trigger per rebuttals.price_estimate_before_design. The rep's actual response ('let me explain how the program works... bill swap') is a reasonable redirect-to-design strategy match, but never flips the $700 bill (once captured) back at the customer as the real cost he's already paying — the flip opportunity is available later and never used.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be judged to have handled this correctly since the canonical rebuttal is redirect-to-design, not a hard flip — the miss is more precisely a bill_anchor flip miss than an objection-handling miss at this exact ts.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to hold the redirect-to-design answer, then bookend it later with an explicit reference to the $700 bill as the answer to 'what's the cost' — cost of NOT switching, not a number the rep invents.

quote: Last month, the last bill I got was $700.
stewart_read: Strong bill capture — a $700 winter bill is exactly the pain-anchor the schema wants. The rep's response ('Woah. Okay.') acknowledges the shock but never flips it into 'that's the amount solar replaces' language for the rest of the call.
coaching_implication: This is the single clearest missed flip on the call — replay ts 01:47 through 02:29 with the rep and show where 'that $700 becomes your solar payment instead' should have landed.

quote: Alright. Well, I don't understand why you can't just give me a general idea of what what we're talking about rather than wasting a lot of time.
stewart_read: Customer is explicitly frustrated by the perceived stall. Rather than re-anchoring to his own $700 bill pain or creating curiosity about his specific savings, the rep repeats the generic 'bunch of different factors' explanation, which reads as friction-management rather than value-creation.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically holding firm on the no-fabricated-numbers rule (schema-correct), so the repetition could be read as disciplined restraint rather than a failure — but the delivery doesn't vary or de-escalate, which is the actual gap.
coaching_implication: Coach a reframe: acknowledge the frustration by name before restating the policy, e.g., naming that the customer feels stalled, then re-anchoring to his own bill number as the reason the specificity matters.

quote: I feel like I'm getting a runaround for, you know, for another reason.
stewart_read: The customer directly states he suspects an ulterior motive — this is a trust-rupture moment, not just a process objection. The rep's next line moves straight back into the on-peak/off-peak technical explanation without acknowledging the suspicion itself.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as a trust_or_scam objection under protocols, but the customer never asks how his info was obtained, so protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number does not apply; this is better read as an unaddressed distrust signal with no current Ion protocol covering it directly — a schema gap worth flagging for Kenny.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to name the distrust directly ('I hear you — it might feel like I'm dodging, I promise I'm not') before re-explaining process; silence on the accusation lets suspicion sit unresolved for several more exchanges.

quote: No. I've looked into it before. As a matter of fact, I currently have a solar panel on the roof, but it only it it's only for hot water, not for electricity.
stewart_read: Customer discloses an existing solar installation. The rep logs it ('Just putting that in my notes here.') but doesn't probe further. This does not trigger orphaned_flow since the existing system is a non-electric solar-thermal unit, not a competing electric solar installation — so no DQ questions apply — but the rep also didn't ask who installed it or whether it affects roof space/orientation for a new electric system.
alternative_hypothesis: Since this isn't a true orphaned-flow trigger (electric solar), the omission is minor; the rep's brief acknowledgment and move-on is arguably adequate for a non-competing system.
coaching_implication: Low-priority: for future calls, note that an existing hot-water solar panel could affect roof space for an electric array — worth one follow-up question for the closer's benefit, not urgent here.

quote: No. I'm just trying to figure out exactly what's going on. If there's no if there's no upfront cost, don't pay anything. Then who's who's paying for installing whatever it is?
stewart_read: This is a financial-mechanism question that the schema flags as closer-tier content, but the rep answers it directly and at length (bill-swap explanation, net metering explanation extending to 11:55) rather than using the escape hatch to route to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be intentionally building trust by demonstrating competence before the appointment, since the customer was already suspicious of a 'runaround' — answering plainly could be read as de-escalation rather than scope creep.
coaching_implication: Coach the universal escape hatch here: 'That's exactly what the specialist walks through on-site' would have protected appointment value while still being responsive; instead the rep gave away net-metering mechanics that the closer would normally use to build value.

quote: Perfect. K. So here's what we'll do. Me and my design team, I'll I'll get everything sent over to them.
stewart_read: After extracting a full year of usage data, the rep pivots straight into scheduling without reflecting any of that data back to the customer as a hook (e.g., noting the summer-to-winter swing or the $700 peak as what the design will target). The data becomes a checkbox rather than a forward-pulling curiosity moment.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged that after the earlier friction, re-litigating the numbers risked reigniting the 'runaround' complaint, so moving straight to booking could be a strategic de-escalation choice.
coaching_implication: Coach a one-line curiosity bridge before offering appointment times: reflect the $700 peak and the swing to $849 at the low point back to the customer as exactly what the design will be built to shrink.
